a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado)
i: e/i — and (variant of e before some sounds) · also i — there, therein (adverb, Latin ibi, like French y; meted i las fedes, 'put your pledged faith into it')
qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied')
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something')
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift')
sancho: Sancho — the abbot of San Pedro de Cardeña
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold')
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least'
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour'
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
prendet: prender — take! (2nd pl. imperative, variant spelling of prended)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira')
pagado: pagar — satisfied, pleased; also paid (past part.; será pagado = 'he will be content with')
conducho: conducho — provisions, victuals (Latin conductus; covers everything an army eats)
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land
marcos: marco — mark (a unit of weight for silver, pl.)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!'
far: far — to do (apocopated infinitive of fazer; = hacer)
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
dinero: dinero — penny (a small coin, the unit of smallest denomination)
doña: doña — lady (title; Latin domina, fem. of don)
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
fagades: fazer — you may make (present subjunctive 2nd pl.; = hagáis)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
recabdo: recabdo — care, precaution, strict order (= recaudo) · also recabdo — business secured, a sure outcome (con todo buen recabdo 'with everything well in hand')
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?')
algo: algo — something; the poem's discreet word for money, wealth
mando: mandar — I promise, vow; I order (present 1st sg.)
gelo: ge + lo — it to him/them (ge, ancestor of modern se, + lo; = se lo)
avie: aver — he had (imperfect; unaccented spelling beside avié)
grado: grado — thanks (grado a … 'thanks be to …') · also grado — will, good will (de grado 'willingly, gladly'; de grado non avrié nada, 'of good will there would be nothing to be had')
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
fincó: fincar — he planted, set firm (preterite; fincar los inojos 'to kneel')
inojos: inojo — knee (= hinojo; fincar los inojos 'to kneel')
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding
canpeador: Campeador — spelling variant with n for m (copyist's spelling) of Campeador, the Cid's epithet
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
fostes: seer — you were (archaic 2nd pl. preterite of ser, used respectfully to one person; = fuestes)
nado: nacer — born (past part.; = nacido); omne nado, 'man born', an all-inclusive idiom like moros nin cristianos
sodes: seer — you are (2nd pl. present, used respectfully to one person; = sois; old -edes ending, cf. odredes, vedes, catedes)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already'
complida: complir — fulfilled, accomplished (past part. fem.; = cumplida)
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us')
hemos: aver — we will/shall (1st pl. future auxiliary; restored by Pidal in the split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
santa: santo — Saint (fem.); Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos
maría: María — Mary; Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como)
veedes: veer — you see (2nd pl. present, old -edes ending; = veis)
y: y — and (rarer spelling of e) · also y — there (adverb, = i, Latin ibi; entraré y 'I shall enter there')
aun: aun — even, besides · also aun — yet, still (aun vea el dia 'may I yet see the day')
ondrada: ondrar — honored, splendid (past part. fem. used as adj.; = honrada)
seades: seer — you may be (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades ending; = seáis)
san: santo — Saint (apocopated before a name; = san)
pero: Pero — Peter (San Pero = San Pedro, the saint of the monastery)
arlançón: Arlançón — the Arlanzón, the river of Burgos
martín: Martín (Antolínez) — a knight of Burgos, companion of the Cid, who provisions him on his exile and negotiates the loan from Raquel and Vidas
antolínez: Antolínez — surname of Martín Antolínez, the Burgalese knight who aids the Cid
ellos: ellos — they, them (stressed 3rd pl. masc. pronoun)
